caption_argument_segments: Deloitte published a piece on the agentic supply chain worth reading if you’re in manufacturing or supply chain.

A few things that stood out: • Agents support a more continuous planning approach through sensing, decision-making, and response instead of waiting on traditional planning cycles. • This isn’t one agent doing everything…
Deloitte also cited Gartner’s projection that ~50% of supply chain management solutions will include agentic AI by 2030. I can see this happening.

Lately I’ve been using Claude to run some simple agents with anonymized data. Things like checking planning data (lead times, purchase order dates, safety stock, etc.), flagging errors, and suggesting corrections based…
It’s still early, though the shift is noticeable from a productivity standpoint.
Curious how much value is showing up in practice for others?
